headline: IIT Mandi launches Science on Wheels for rural students in Himachal Pradesh
content: The Indian Institute of Technology Mandi, in partnership with Plaksha University and the Igniting Dreams of Young Minds Foundation, has launched the Science on Wheels programme in Himachal Pradesh to promote practical science education among school students, news agency Press Trust of India reported.Supported by the Department of Science and Technology, Government of India, the programme aims to help students, particularly those in rural areas, understand the difference between classroom learning and scientific experiments.The Himachal Pradesh leg of the programme was launched on October 17 at IIT Mandi Campus School in the presence of the institute's director, Professor Laxmidhar Behera, officials told PTI.After reaching more than 7,500 students across 70 schools in Chhattisgarh and Punjab, the initiative plans to cover 50 schools in Himachal Pradesh. These include schools in Mandi, Kullu, Bilaspur, Hamirpur and Kangra.Following the launch, the team began its work in Mandi district by visiting government senior secondary schools in Badog, Baggi (K), Bari Gumanu, Batheri and Deori.The programme is for students from Classes VI to XII. It offers about six hours of learning activities at each school under four themes: space technology, robotics, sustainability and water filtration."Science on Wheels is a great initiative. We need to develop an interest in science amongst our children as they are the future of an Atmanirbhar Bharat," Behera said, according to PTI.He said the programme would encourage students to learn science and added that they could develop futuristic technology in India.Science on Wheels will seek to take practical science education to 50 schools across five districts of Himachal Pradesh after reaching more than 7,500 students in Chhattisgarh and Punjab.- Ends

headline: IIT Mandi launches ‘Science on Wheels’ initiative to reach 50 schools across Himachal
content: Mandi (Himachal Pradesh) [India], October 26 (ANI): The Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Mandi has launched the Department of Science and Technology (DST)-supported ‘Science on Wheels’ initiative to promote hands-on science education among students in 50 schools across Himachal Pradesh.Developed in collaboration with Plaksha University and the Igniting Dreams of Young Minds (IDYM) Foundation, the mobile science education programme aims to bridge the gap between theoretical learning and practical experimentation for students from Classes 6 to 12.Following successful rollouts in Chhattisgarh and Punjab, the initiative has now been extended to Himachal Pradesh, where it will cover schools in districts including Mandi, Kullu, Bilaspur, Hamirpur and Kangra.Each school visit will feature an intensive six-hour programme, offering students interactive learning experiences in space technology, robotics, sustainability and water filtration. The initiative is designed to encourage scientific curiosity, critical thinking and experiential learning among schoolchildren.The programme was inaugurated by IIT Mandi Director Laxmidhar Behera at the IIT Mandi Campus School. A major highlight of the launch was a live hydro-rocket demonstration, which illustrated scientific principles such as force, pressure and motion through a practical experiment.The initiative is being led by Rucha Joshi of Plaksha University, in collaboration with IIT Mandi and the IDYM Foundation, which is associated with the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO).Supported by the DST, the programme seeks to make science education more accessible and engaging for students, particularly by providing exposure to experiments and technology-based activities that may not be readily available in conventional classrooms.Through its mobile outreach model, ‘Science on Wheels’ aims to strengthen scientific awareness among school students and inspire them to explore science, technology and innovation through practical learning. (ANI)

Bank holiday today: Are banks open or closed due to Valmiki Jayanti 2026?
content: Banks in many states will be closed today, on Monday, October 26, due to Valmiki Jayanti 2026. Therefore, bank customers should schedule their branch visits accordingly. For the majority of regular transactions, consumers in such regions can still use online banking, mobile banking apps, and the Unified Payments Interface (UPI). The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has specified which days in October 2026 banks in various states will not be open for physical operations.Valmiki Jayanti bank holiday 2026Bank branches will be closed in Tripura, Chandigarh, Jammu, Himachal Pradesh, Shimla, and Srinagar. Both public and private banks in these states are covered by the vacation. SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, PNB, and Canara Bank are some among these. Before visiting, customers should check the holiday schedule at their local branch. Not all of India is affected by today's holiday. Along with national holidays and normal weekly holidays, banks recognize regional celebrations and holidays. This explains why certain branches do not open on Mondays. In January, the RBI publishes its official list of yearly bank holidays.Banking services on Valmiki Jayanti 2026 bank holidayDuring branch holidays, online banking provides ways to make payments. Customers can send and receive money via the bank's app or UPI. These services are available 24/7, including on holidays. However, access may be momentarily disrupted by planned maintenance. Customers are informed about such maintenance by banks. Online banking also allows customers to access their accounts. Holidays under the Negotiable Instruments Act and Banks' Closing of Accounts are marked on the RBI calendar. Customers can schedule visits to services that need branch support by checking local holiday specifics.What is next for the Bank holiday in Oct 2026?The stated holidays are observed by all banks, both planned and unscheduled. Shimla branches will close for Karva Chauth on October 29 after today. On October 31, Ahmedabad branches will be closed in honor of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's birthday. When scheduling branch visits, customers in these cities should take these dates into account.

headline: UNA 2026 Annual General Meeting starts on October 27
content: United Nurses of Alberta’s three-day 2026 Annual General Meeting begins on Tuesday, October 27 in Edmonton. The theme of this year’s meeting is “Your Nurses, Your Future.” Including delegates, observers, staff, and representatives of other unions and organizations, more than 1,000 delegates, staff, guests and observers are expected to attend the event at Edmonton EXPO Centre. On the first day of the session, delegates will hear reports from UNA President Heather Smith, Secretary-Treasurer Christina Doktor and Labour Relations Director David Harrigan, as well as guest speaker Chris Gallaway from Friends of Medicare. Later during the AGM, elections will be held for the position of Second Vice-President and regional district representatives. In a closed-door session at the end of the day Tuesday, members will have the opportunity to question the Executive Board about the administration of the union. On Wednesday, delegates will hear from guest speakers, Canadian Federation of Nurses Unions President Linda Silas and University of Alberta Professor Health Law and Science Policy Timothy Caulfield.

headline: Una Terra Appoints Former Sealed Air CEO William Hickey as Operating Partner
content: Una Terra, an investment firm focused on the circular economy, has appointed William “Bill” Hickey, former President, CEO and Chairman of Sealed Air Corporation, as Operating Partner. Hickey brings more than 30 years of industrial leadership experience, including senior executive responsibilities in manufacturing, packaging, product innovation and corporate operations. Based in New York City, Hickey will work directly with Una Terra’s portfolio companies to support business expansion, operational improvements and entry into the U.S. market. His appointment strengthens the firm’s operational capabilities as it invests in companies developing solutions for sustainable packaging, materials innovation and the broader circular economy. Hickey spent more than 30 years at Sealed Air Corporation, a global packaging company specializing in food protection and protective packaging solutions. During his tenure, he advanced through several senior leadership positions, beginning as a division general manager before becoming Chief Financial Officer and Chief Operating Officer.

headline: Bank peon arrested over Rs 20 lakh government jobs scam in Himachal
content: A woman bank employee accused of cheating unemployed youths of about Rs 20 lakh by promising them government jobs has been arrested in Himachal Pradesh's Hamirpur district, PTI reported.The woman, who allegedly works as a peon at a bank, was arrested on October 24 and is being questioned in connection with a fraud case registered at Hamirpur's Sadar Police Station.Police said courts in Rampur, Hamirpur and Jhanduta had issued non-bailable warrants against her. They have not disclosed her identity as the interrogation is under way.The case came to light after a young man accused the woman of fraud, Hamirpur Additional Superintendent of Police Rajesh Kumar told PTI. Police subsequently received complaints from several other people.The woman, a resident of Hamirpur district, allegedly took lakhs of rupees from youths and their families after assuring them that she could secure government jobs for them.She had also allegedly promised jobs to people in the Palampur and Rampur areas. When the jobs did not materialise, the victims sought refunds, but she allegedly kept delaying repayment.As pressure to return the money mounted, the woman allegedly issued cheques to the victims. The cheques bounced because her account had insufficient funds, police said.Kumar said police were investigating whether other people were involved in the alleged scam. The woman remains under questioning over allegations that she collected about Rs 20 lakh by promising government jobs.- Ends
